chunks: And whatever is narrated from Muhammad ibn Uthman Al-Amri - may Allah sanctify his soul - I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with them - from Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Uthman Al-Amri - may Allah sanctify his soul.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to the narrator's father (often a scholar himself)
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: May Allah be pleased with them, an honorific for the narrators
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ الْحِمِيرِي: Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ: May Allah sanctify his soul, an honorific for deceased scholars
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ الْعَمِيرِيُّ: Muhammad ibn Uthman Al-Amri, a prominent Shia scholar and narrator

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the chain for Muhammad ibn Uthman Al-Amri's hadith?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous chain-of-transmission (isnad) methodology central to Shia hadith scholarship, specifically within Shaykh al-Saduq's *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By explicitly linking the narrator to his father and other key figures like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, it establishes the reliability and scholarly lineage of the reports attributed to Muhammad ibn Uthman Al-Amri, a prominent companion of the Imams.
